methodology.gateDefinition: PASS means reviewed public identity/kind, core descriptions/highlights, admission interpretation and opening-hours assertions have no known contradiction after repair; explicit unavailable/unknown values pass only when not presented as free, zero, or a verified specific value. This does not certify full planning readiness, image content/licensing, exact coordinates, or route accuracy.
nonGoals: Do not fill unknown admission, transport, parking or seasonality values with guesses.
Do not change recommendation, budget or comfort formulas.
Do not certify routes from the derived estimates.
Do not validate image subject or licenses by visual inspection in this audit.
Do not geocode or certify exact coordinate placement.
Do not update Notion or create follow-up issues.
Do not treat manifest validation as independent source-truth verification or automatic outcome adjudication.
methodology.outcomeAdjudication: PASS/FAIL labels are manually adjudicated row by row against cited source observations and the stated gate. The audit script replays the frozen base-to-candidate edits and checks source references, counts, hashes, and report freshness; it does not re-fetch source pages or mechanically recompute those judgments.

sourceAccess.method: one-time manual consultation of official operator/municipal/visitor-guide pages; no recurring fetch or source scraping
sourceAccess.robotsAndTerms: not systematically reviewed for every source; no automation or recurring reuse is authorized by this report

excludedSources.observation: The site footer restricts reuse of its information/images without authorization. It was excluded from evidence used for the revised Fushimi record.

sources.observation: Municipal information identifies Shinjuku City as a Tokyo ward and describes its position among Tokyo’s 23 cities.

sources.authority: GO TOKYO / Tokyo Convention & Visitors Bureau
sources.observation: Visitor guide describes the Shinjuku district and named observatory features; its around-the-clock wording is not treated as every venue’s schedule.

sources.authority: Kyoto City Tourism Association — Kyoto City Official Guide
sources.observation: Official guide gives Kyoto’s historic-capital context and distinguishes heritage sites within city limits.
Official tourism guide describes Osaka as a major urban and historic economic/cultural center.
Official destination guide identifies Lake Ashi, Hakone Shrine, Owakudani and Hakone Open-Air Museum as area features.
Municipal site identifies Hakone Town and its official address; it does not establish a town-wide visitor schedule.
Municipal tourism listing identifies Kumoba Pond in Karuizawa and does not assign it a fixed opening schedule.
Official fee page lists the 150 m Main Deck, 09:00–23:00 hours, 22:30 last admission, and ¥1,500 adult ticket.
Official calendar for 2026-10-05 shows 10:00–22:00 hours, last admission 21:00, and warns hours may change.
Official ticket page identifies the Tembo Deck product and an adult starting price; date-selected fares are not a fixed amount.
Official visitor page says grounds are free and gates follow seasonal sunrise/sunset; internal facilities can have shorter hours and separate fees.

sources.authority: GO TOKYO / Tokyo Convention & Visitors Bureau
sources.observation: Official Tokyo guide locates Shibuya Scramble Crossing outside Shibuya Station.

sources.authority: GO TOKYO / Tokyo Convention & Visitors Bureau
sources.observation: Official guide locates the Hachiko Statue near Shibuya Scramble Crossing.

Official Tokyo Metropolitan Park Association page states the park is continuously open (常時開園), notes service-center and facility closures during year-end/New Year, directs users to inquire about operating hours, and identifies paid facilities.

sources.authority: Kyoto City and Kyoto City Tourism Association — Kyoto Travel
sources.observation: Official guide identifies Fushimi Inari Taisha as a shrine, describes a hillside path with over 5,000 torii gates and fox statues, and does not list general visitor hours or an admission amount.

sources.authority: Shokoku-ji Religious Corporation — official Kinkaku-ji site
sources.observation: Official English access page lists 09:00–17:00 visits year-round, notes hours may change for special exhibitions, and lists 250-car parking, parking hours 08:40–17:10, and passenger-car fees of ¥400 for the first 60 minutes then ¥200 per additional 30 minutes.
Official 2026 schedule lists seasonal opening/closing hours; the reviewed page does not state an ordinary general-admission amount.
Official FAQ confirms hours vary seasonally and refers users to visitor guidance; it gives no standard fee amount.

sources.authority: Kyoto City — official Nijo-jo Castle site
sources.observation: Official site distinguishes 08:45–16:00 entry from 17:00 closure and lists separate tickets for castle and palace.

sources.authority: Kyoto City and Kyoto City Tourism Association — Kyoto Travel
sources.observation: Official area guide identifies the Bamboo Forest and Togetsu-kyo Bridge as Saga/Arashiyama features; the area has no single facility schedule.

sources.authority: Osaka Castle Main Tower — official operator
sources.observation: Official page lists 09:00–18:00 hours, 17:30 last admission, and ¥1,200 general adult Main Tower admission.
Official page describes a Pacific Ocean exhibit journey, variable date-based pricing and a calendar; on 2026-10-05 it showed age 16+ admission ¥2,800 and 10:30–20:00 hours.
Official Dotonbori listing describes a shopping/business district and says store business hours vary.

sources.authority: The Hakone Open-Air Museum — official operator
sources.observation: Official page lists 09:00–17:00, 16:30 last admission, year-round schedule, adult same-day ¥2,000 and online ¥1,800.

sources.authority: The Hakone Open-Air Museum — official collection page
sources.observation: Official collection page describes about 100 outdoor modern/contemporary masterpieces and a Picasso collection exceeding 300 works.
Official destination listing describes Kyu-Karuizawa Ginza as a roughly 750 m shopping street with bakeries, cafés and eateries.

sources.authority: Shokoku-ji Religious Corporation — official Kinkaku-ji Japanese access page
sources.observation: Official Japanese access page lists parking 08:40–17:10; 250 spaces across lots 1–3; passenger-car fees ¥400 for the first 60 minutes and ¥200 per additional 30 minutes; visiting hours 09:00–17:00 year-round.
